newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Convict tries to blast out of Bogota jail with grenade.
newsitem.headline: Convict tries to blast out of Bogota jail with grenade.

text.p: A convict tried to blast his way out of Bogota's high-security Modelo jail armed with a grenade and a .22 pistol early on Monday, the head of the National Prisons Institute (INPEC) said.

The man, who was serving time for firearms offences, sawed through the bars of his cell and escaped into the patio about 3 a.m. (0800 GMT). He then lobbed a grenade at a guard post that exploded causing damage but no injuries, national prisons chief Col. Rafael Pardo told the Radionet radio network.
Reporters at the scene spoke of two explosions inside the prison compound but Pardo did not explain the cause of the second blast. Pardo did not say how the prisoner had been recaptured.

"We're investigating to see how this man broke out and how he had time to saw through the bars of his cell during the night. It seems that he tried to face the guard down with the grenade and a .22 pistol. He threw the grenade at the guard post but there was no serious damage," Pardo told Radionet.

The escape attempt comes against the backdrop of a recent series of incidents that has highlighted unrest and lax security in a number of Colombia's jails -- including riots, an underground tunnel that was to be used for an escape bid and even a flock of carrier pigeons that were being used to fly drugs to inmates at one prison.
